clue.text: Answer in pamphlet makes one carry on

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political
ANS is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Finding the answer printed in a leaflet spurs someone to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: ANS is a common crossword abbreviation for answer; 'carry on' here means conduct, as in carrying on business.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to conduct or carry it on, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Lead in this getting Oscar? Fine film

indicators.note: the lead of a word is the letter at its front, so only the initial is used

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Asks whether the star of this movie will win an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Hat is the 1935 Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is a classic Hollywood musical, so the answer is an example of a film.

clue.text: Immediately pay the penalty, catching cold

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to atone is to make amends or pay for wrongdoing
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Paying a price straight away for catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: At once is a phrase meaning without delay, a synonym of right now.

clue.text: Select cap randomly from display

indicators.note: random means in no set order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Picking a hat at random from a shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public show or display.

clue.text: Tosca part he turned into a disaster

indicators.note: something turned is changed around, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A singer made a fiasco of a role in Puccini's opera Tosca.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden great misfortune, a synonym of calamity.

clue.text: Watches a woman's first swing

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of woman is used

explanation.surface: Someone observes a woman's first go on a swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank that swings up and down, so it is a kind of swing.

clue.text: Choice of the Spanish, Italian, and English

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Picking between Spanish, Italian and English options.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the pick of a group, the best, as choice is used for the select few.

clue.text: Order changed for cashmere? I haven't a clue

indicators.note: a changed order means the sequence is altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asked why an order was switched to cashmere confesses ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an informal idiom meaning I do not know.

clue.text: Section of orchestra producing 'Merry Widow' on record, ultimately

indicators.note: a merry person is tipsy and unsteady, so the letters are jumbled
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is used

explanation.surface: Part of an orchestra recording Lehár's operetta The Merry Widow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry Widow' reads as the operetta title, but Merry is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodwind are the flutes, oboes, clarinets and bassoons, one of the orchestra's sections.

clue.text: Asset for forward having extra yard

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
forward in the sense of cheeky or impudent
Y is the abbreviation for yard, added on at the end

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a football forward whose extra yard of pace is an asset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a football position but means saucy, as in pert.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is something owned, and anything owned of value is an asset.

clue.text: Group of stars interrupted by a bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Virgo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Stargazing interrupted by a grumpy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, ill-tempered woman; the word is a dictionary synonym of shrew.

clue.text: A Highlander in a cravat

parts.note: a Highlander comes from the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: A Scotsman wearing a cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neck scarf or tie, a type of cravat, named after the racecourse.

clue.text: One unreasonably held to be above criticism in case, crowd stoned

definitions.text: One unreasonably held to be above criticism

indicators.note: someone stoned is intoxicated and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone thought above reproach is pelted with stones by a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idiom for an institution or person treated as immune from criticism.

clue.text: Find me working in food game

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the shuffled piece goes within

parts.note: cheer in the old sense of food and drink, as in good cheer

indicators.note: working means in operation or being processed, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A request to be found at work in the food trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheer once meant food and drink provided, as in 'good cheer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemin de fer is a card game, a variant of baccarat.

clue.text: Prostitute's toms, carnal we suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A sleazy reading about a sex worker's clients being up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toms' is slang for prostitutes, helping the surface, but here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet woman is an old, biblical-flavoured idiom for a harlot or immoral woman.

clue.text: They may be provided for the rest of the train's passengers

definitions.text: They may be provided for the rest of the train's passengers

parts.words: They may be provided for the rest of the train's passengers
parts.note: surface reading: something supplied for the remaining people aboard a train
setter's reading: rest means sleep, so these are railway sleeping cars

explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' looks like 'the remainder' but means repose; the answer is the French term for sleeping carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons-lits are continental railway sleeping cars, provided so passengers can sleep overnight.

clue.text: Admiral at sea penning good song

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, so one piece is enclosed by the other
being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A naval officer on a voyage writes a fine song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' suggests composing, fitting the song, but here it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Statuette, popular in price

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so that piece goes within

parts.note: a figure is a sum or price

explanation.surface: A small statue that is well-liked and well-priced.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurine is a small carved or moulded figure, the same as a statuette.

clue.text: Girl phones about empty shop in a town down under

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the girl and phones sit on either side of the next piece
an empty word has its insides cleared out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A girl calls about a deserted shop in an Australian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl phones' is read as one unit that sits either side of the emptied shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in Australia's Northern Territory; down under is slang for Australia.

clue.text: Person takes long time going round wine shop

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person

indicators.note: going round means turning to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone spends ages wandering around an off-licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or wine shop.

clue.text: Season the Italian vegetable

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season before Easter

explanation.surface: Seasoning an Italian vegetable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a cooking verb but is a period of the church year.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is a small edible pulse, a seed counted among vegetables.

clue.text: Parliamentarian's stout leader

parts.note: stout and round both mean plump

explanation.surface: A member of parliament has a portly chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were the Parliamentarian side in the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundhead was the nickname for a supporter of Parliament against Charles I in the 1640s.

clue.text: Tipple before a play

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A drink before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for stage or screen.

clue.text: Snare large deer (name for male)

indicators.note: one thing for another means it stands in its place, so one letter replaces the other

parts.note: the moose is the largest deer
N is the abbreviation for name
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Catching a big stag, with a note about naming the male.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of MOOSE is swapped for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a running loop of rope, the kind used to trap animals as a snare.

clue.text: Uniform worn by soldier, and sailor with axe

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone goes around them, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A uniformed soldier and a sailor armed with an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Axe is musicians' slang for a guitar, especially an electric one.

clue.text: A female, articulate and wealthy

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Describes a woman who is well-spoken and rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means having plenty of money, a straightforward synonym of rich.

clue.text: Place containing small back room

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to lay something is to place it

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: A building with a little back room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun but is the verb lay; 'room' means scope, not a chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom to manoeuvre, as in room or margin for action.

clue.text: Humiliating blunder made by fool getting fine in front of everybody

parts.note: prat is British slang for an idiot
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An idiot is fined publicly after an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pratfall is literally a fall on the buttocks, and figuratively an embarrassing mistake.
